corpus.statement: TEN DOCUMENTS IS THE CORPUS, and it stays ten until more notices are ingested. This is an enumeration, not an estimate. It was 8 until 2026-10-10: on 2026-09-30 all six sandbox MinIO buckets were listed in full (4061 objects), every PDF under every sustainment prefix was fetched and hashed, and the result was 8 distinct document contents with no unseen notice sitting in the bucket -- enumerated in docs/pcn-corpus-widening-2026-09-30.md. The corpus therefore does not widen by looking harder; it widens when new notices are ingested, which is exactly how it reached 10. TI PCN#20210316000.1 and IDT/Renesas PDN OV-19-05 were ingested into sustainment/inbound/ on 2026-10-10, the sustainment_sensor fired on both unaided, and both produced manifests under the versioned artifact layout.
corpus.why_it_is_here: This block exists so the denominator lives where the GATE READS IT rather than only in prose. pcn_corpus_run.check_ground_truth() asserts TARGETS against it at startup and aborts on a disagreement, and pcn_corpus_gate.py copies it into docs/corpus-gate/latest.json so a committed report states the corpus it was measured against. A denominator that only a human can check is a denominator that drifts.
corpus.source_sha256_rekey_note: THE CORPUS IS KEYED BY SOURCE CONTENT HASH (sha256), not by filename. Re-keyed 2026-10-12. Diodes_PCN_2683_Rev1_EOL.pdf and Diodes_PCN_2683_FULLGREEN.pdf are ONE document under two filenames: byte-identical, measured 2026-10-12 inside the sandbox doc-tools pod, both 181899 bytes, both sha256 af5bfad3f9344eb1dc942230a33cb61b58fb911b977da2063fffbecb5788074c (md5 abe083fe...). Exactly one filename, Diodes_PCN_2683_Rev1_EOL.pdf, is SCORED; Diodes_PCN_2683_FULLGREEN.pdf is a DECLARED ALIAS -- listed in documents[] so a fire of either name is anchored to the declared bytes, asserted rather than double-scored, and absent from notices{} and from TARGETS. Until this re-key that document was scored twice at 402 parts, which is why the harness reported 924 ground-truth parts over 522 distinct ones: 402 of the 924, 77% of the distinct corpus, was one document counted twice. gt_parts == distinct_parts == 522 now holds BY ASSERTION (pcn_corpus_run.check_ground_truth aborts the run if it ever stops holding), so a divergence means a new duplicate document entered the corpus or a part number is shared across two notices, and both need a ruling before a score is quoted. 896, 898 and 924 are HISTORICAL denominators: reports predating 2026-10-12 keep theirs, and a score must always be cited with its denominator. The superseded note said "Keep the duplicate pair -- it is how the two-ingest case is exercised". That was wrong: scoring one document twice does not exercise two ingests, it inflates one document to 77% of the corpus. The two-ingest case is now exercised by the declared alias plus the per-fire declared-bytes check (pcn_corpus_gate.check_declared_bytes). The removed notices{} entry for the alias was identical to the Rev1_EOL entry in count (402), mpns (same 402, set-equal), malformed and headers (both empty); it differed only in manifest and source. Its manifest key, preserved here so the second ingest is not lost from the record, was: sustainment/inbound/generated/Diodes_PCN_2683_FULLGREEN_pdf/manifest.json. Four S3 keys hold these bytes (see inbound_copies on the document entry).

documents.inbound_copies_note: Corrected 3 -> 4 on 2026-10-12 from a measurement, not a tune: four S3 keys hold these bytes -- sustainment/inbound/Diodes_PCN_2683_FULLGREEN.pdf, sustainment/inbound/diodes_2683/Diodes_PCN_2683_Rev1_EOL.pdf, sustainment/inbound/diodes_bbox/Diodes_PCN_2683_Rev1_EOL.pdf, sustainment/inbound/diodes_tier1/Diodes_PCN_2683_Rev1_EOL.pdf. The declared 3 counted only the Rev1_EOL prefixes and missed the root FULLGREEN copy.

corpus.widens_when: A new notice is ingested into processing-artifacts/sustainment/inbound/**. Then: add its TARGETS row, add its part numbers to notices{} under the same verbatim-presence rule as every other entry, and raise scored_entries / distinct_documents / gt_parts / distinct_parts here. Re-enumerating the bucket does NOT widen it -- that was done, and found nothing new.
